claims.content: To aid Customer Service Reps in troubleshooting customer service issues by providing access to the Customer History Page.

goal.raw_text: To aid Customer Service Reps in troubleshooting customer service issues by providing access to the Customer History Page.

claims.content: Customer Service Representative
The Customer Service Representative must have access to the Customer History Page.
The Customer Service Representative must be able to search for customer accounts using e-mail address, phone number, or customer name.
The system must display customer account information including Last Name, First Name, City, ST, Zip, Phone, E-mail address, and buttons for Bid History, Order History, View Notes, and Reset Password.
If the account is deactivated, it must be listed in RED on the Customer History Page.
A customer contacts Customer Service with an inquiry regarding their auction activity or account status.

trigger.raw_text: A customer contacts Customer Service with an inquiry regarding their auction activity or account status.

claims.content: The Customer Service Representative searches for the customer account using e-mail address, phone number, or customer name.
The system displays the 'Results' section including Last Name, First Name, City, ST, Zip, Phone, E-mail address, and buttons for Bid History, Order History, View Notes, and Reset Password.
If the account is deactivated, it is listed in RED on the Customer History Page.
The Customer Service Representative clicks the appropriate button (Bid History, Order History, or View Notes) to navigate to the relevant section using anchor tags.

The system displays the selected section: Bid History includes item’s closing date/time, auction sequence numbers, product ID (SKU), customer’s last bid, SmartBid (if placed), and winning bid; Order History includes order dates, auction sequence numbers, product ID (SKU), order amounts, and status; View Notes allows free-form text entry by CSRs.
If the Customer Service Representative attempts to deactivate an account, a pop-up DIV layer will appear asking for a supervisor's authorization code.
Only supervisors will know these codes, which are issued by Administrators and generated by the Auction Admin application; Supervisors do not need Administrator access to input the codes.
Deactivating an Account will require a Supervisor's authorization code as indicated in the mockup.

If a Customer Service Representative attempts to deactivate an account without providing a valid supervisor authorization code, the system will not proceed with deactivation and will require the correct code to be entered.

Only supervisors possess knowledge of the authorization codes required for account deactivation; if a non-supervisor CSR attempts entry, the action cannot be completed until a supervisor provides the code.
The Customer Service Representative has successfully accessed and reviewed the customer’s Bid History, Order History, or Account Notes as needed to resolve the inquiry.
If the account was deactivated during the session, it is now listed in RED on the Customer History Page and requires supervisor authorization for reactivation.
Any notes entered by the CSR into the free-form Account Notes section are saved and visible for future reference.
The system has not allowed any new account creation using an email address that already exists on the blacklist, if such a check was performed during the investigation.
